notes: Identity assessment: this canonical text concatenates two substantive constituent primary replication reports, not one report bearing the supplied Tyner, Loomas, Miske, Luis, and Kline Struhl authorship. Introductory provenance names the matching King_JournOrgBehavior_2017_Q1dl project (ndbrp), states the supplied 9bkuf file returns HTTP 410, and identifies constituent projects xzufr and hq4cr. Both reports identify King & Bryant (2017), Journal of Organizational Behavior, Study 3, and the WICS incremental-validity claim. The second prints DOI 10.1002/job.2118. Candidate A names Marie Juanchich and Daniel Jolles as contributors; candidate B names Zachariah Berry and Berry_om7 / hq4cr. These are primary results reports rather than abstracts or preregistrations, but the input provides no constituent-specific locator; cache naming/provenance cannot establish row correspondence. No supplied PDF; no rendering. Candidate A (78xj3): WICS added to hierarchical regression controlling demographics, JSS, SIC and AOWS; explicit analytic participant N=183, after excluding 3 attention-check failures and collecting additional responses. Printed F(1,175)=26.03, p<.001, ΔR2=.11; Cohen's f2=.12; WICS β=.45, p<.001. Authors explicitly call replication successful. Candidate B (acdve): WICS added to hierarchical regression controlling demographics, job satisfaction, mentoring status, intergenerational tension and age-based work stereotypes; explicit analytic participant N=183. There were 22 under-41 participants re-sampled (18 initially, 4 replacements); preliminary analysis at n=171 preceded extra recruitment to final sample. Printed F(1,175)=47.83, p=.00000000008394, f2=.27; additional unique variance 18%. Authors explicitly call replication successful. Common analytic N=183 retained only as candidate evidence for parent field-scope review. No N derivation or effect-size conversion. No target selected by order or numerical coincidence. Original side is an unassigned placeholder.
